title: Earliest Finish
statement: A renovation has n jobs numbered 0 to n − 1. Job i takes days[i] days, and rules [before, after] say a job can only start once another has finished. Any number of jobs can run at the same time. The rules never form a loop. Return the fewest days to finish every job.

answerKey.pattern: Longest path in a DAG: process jobs in topological order and track each job's finish time
keyPoints: finish[j] = days[j] + the latest finish among jobs that must come before j
Kahn's algorithm gives an order where those are already known
The answer is the largest finish time
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Simulate day by day: O(total days · n)

hints: When can job j start at the earliest?
When the last of its required jobs has finished.
Kahn's order; start[j] = max(finish of predecessors); answer = max finish.
